method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. A script decoded each registrar, callback, vftable cell and call site from those bytes and asserted the addresses recorded in the rows. Callers and stores were enumerated from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. The MEASURED facts come from the call-site index xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json and from the Lua 5.1 bytecode of the installed client scripts, decoded with tools/decode_lpb.py and read as constants and instructions. The script bodies are not tracked, so a MEASURED script fact is reproduced by decoding the named chunk. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: The static Lua call contract of the Global native _createActor for every class kind that the shipped scripts create, with the class kind dispatch through vftable slot +0x6C of the class prototype, the objects that the creation allocates, the _onInit hand-off, the resume checker, the return and the failure paths. The record also gives the contract of the script method AreaBaseClass._loadSpreadSheetPermanently, which consumes the sheet controls that _createActor makes. The record does not describe sheet content, widget layout or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

executeParameters.claim: The callback keeps the ExecuteParameters pointer in ESI. Its +0x04 field is the engine context C, +0x08 is the thread context T, +0x10 is the argument cell holder and +0x1C is the return container that the pushers write. C holds the manager M as its first dword. The Global receiver arrives in ECX and is kept at stack +0x28.

lookups.claim: Four helpers on C reach the manager registry. 0x00CC7A00 finds or creates the record for a name through 0x00CD8870 with create set to 1 and returns the first dword of the record, the control. 0x00CD8870 maps the name to a key through the name table at M +0x18 with 0x00CEDE40 and finds the record in the map at M +0x17C with 0x00D0A2B0. 0x00CC7200 tests that a record exists, through 0x00CD9C60 and 0x00CD8870 with create set to 0. 0x00CC7A50 resolves an identity to a control through the same map at M +0x17C. 0x00CC73B0 builds an identity from a control by reading the dword at +0x70 of the record that 0x00CD7A30 returns for the control.
0x00CD7A30 returns 0 for a null control without a fault. 0x00CC7030 reads the dword at +0x70 of its this pointer without a null test.

registryRecord.claim: The record that 0x00CD8870 returns is the BCS-S-0052 registry entry. This record uses these fields: +0x00 control pointer, +0x08 kind tag, +0x0C record link, +0x70 identity, +0x74 and +0x78 word counters, +0x7A creation flag, +0x7B and +0x7C class style bytes, +0x7D valid byte and +0x7F active byte. 0x00CE2BC0 initializes a record with the kind tag 0x00010007 from 0x0130D4F8, +0x7B, +0x7C and +0x7F set to 1 and the counters and +0x7D cleared. 0x00CE16C0 is true for the kind tags in the cells 0x0130D4FC, 0x0130D500 and 0x0130D504, which hold 0x00010008 to 0x0001000A.

classPrototypes.claim: The record of a class name holds a prototype control as its first dword. The native class table registrar 0x0075F9B0 builds it. For each native class it allocates the native object, runs its constructor and passes the class name, the parent name and the object to 0x00CC9700. A class without its own object goes through 0x00CC9760, which reaches the class definition routine 0x00CD91E0. That routine clones the parent prototype for the child through 0x00CE2D50. A script _defineClass therefore gives a class the native type of the nearest ancestor that has a prototype.

Creating an instance calls virtual slot +4 of the prototype through the thunk 0x00CCC9B0. The slot is the new-object routine of the native type. The record allocator 0x00CE2D50 then allocates a 0x84 byte record, runs 0x00CE2BC0, stores the class record at +0x0C of the new record and sets +0x7A to 1.

The shipped scripts call _defineClass 2435 times and _defineBaseClass 139 times. 182 distinct class names descend from WidgetBaseClass through those calls, counting AskBaseClass itself. By transitive closure over the (child, parent) pairs of the calls, 1 is AskBaseClass, 128 descend from WidgetBaseClass only, 44 from AskBaseClass only and 9 are defined under both WidgetBaseClass and AskBaseClass in different chunks. 53 therefore descend from AskBaseClass and 138 are direct children of WidgetBaseClass. AskBaseClass is defined with _defineBaseClass and parent WidgetBaseClass. No defined class has SpreadSheet, CutScene, DesktopUtil or DesktopWidget as its parent.

resumeResultCells.claim: The result cells are the ones that manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json records. 0x01377ECC holds 0 for done, 0x0130CECC holds 1 for still waiting and 0x0130CED0 holds 2 for a thread without a checker.

scriptBinding.descriptor: _createActor_inl returns the receiver selector global and the name _createActor_cpp

rows.callbackKind: direct member function of the Global holder

arguments.handlerRead: A nil cell, tag 6, substitutes the empty string object at 0x01377E78. Any other cell goes through 0x0071CE70 tag 3.
arguments.note: An empty or nil name asks the creation core to generate a name. A missing argument is padded with a tag 6 cell by the marshaller.

arguments.role: Class name looked up in the class registry.
arguments.note: A mismatched tag reaches the type error route 0x00CCA730 of the marshaller.

arguments.handlerRead: A nil cell skips the read and takes the creation branch. Otherwise 0x0071BA00 tag 2.
arguments.role: Reuse an existing control of the same name.

arguments.handlerRead: 0x00753B90 copies the cells from index 3 on and 0x00791110 converts them.
arguments.role: Payload that the creation hands to _onInit.
arguments.note: The existing-control branch ignores the payload.

returns.note: One value, pushed at once on the ready existing-control branch and by the checker slot 2 after the wait on every other branch. Slot 2 runs only on the done result. A control that is gone at the poll takes 0x00CCE1C0, which ends the thread with no value.

rows.behavior: Reads a name, a class name, a reuse flag and a payload. With the reuse flag set and a control of that name registered, it returns that control, after a wait if the control is not ready. Otherwise it asks the prototype of the class to create a control of the native kind of the class. The creation registers the control under an identity, runs the class _onInit with the payload and returns the control after the resume checker answers. Only the kinds in classKinds have a creator. The call always yields on every branch except a ready existing control.
rows.yieldsNote: Every branch yields except the ready existing control.

branches.condition: Reuse flag true, name registered and control ready
branches.note: No yield and no ownership map entry.

branches.condition: Reuse flag true, name registered and control not ready
pushes: LuaControl*: the existing control, after the checker answers
branches.note: Wait path with an ownership map entry.

branches.condition: Reuse flag false or nil, or name not registered, and a class kind with a creator
pushes: LuaControl*: the new control, after the checker answers
branches.note: Slot +0x6C creates the control and the same wait path follows.

branches.condition: Class kind without a creator, or a creation that fails
branches.note: Slot +0x6C returns 0 for a kind without a creator. A creation fails when the class is not instantiable or when an explicit name is already a global or a registered name, and the core then returns 0 to the unchecked tail. The outcome after that fault was not run.

stateReads.role: Selects which readiness test the checker applies.

stateReads.target: Control record of the existing or new control
stateReads.role: Ready byte that the checker reads when the probe byte is clear. Its only writer is 0x00CE1DD0 and the creation path does not call it.

stateWrites.effect: Inserts the control identity under the key of the creating thread, erased at the resume.
Registers the new control under an allocated identity, or under 0xC0000005 for CutScene.
Explicit-name creation sets globals[name] to the instance table by a raw set. Creation fails instead when that global is already non-nil.

rows.evidenceTier: STATIC for the registration, call sequence, virtual dispatch and checker. MEASURED for the script call shapes. INFERRED where a fact says so. unknown where a fact says so.

facts.claim: The registrar 0x00757350 pushes the name literal 0x00FD85DC at 0x00757439 and loads the callback 0x00709640 into ESI at 0x00757387. It calls the return list builder 0x0072C260, the argument list builder 0x007407A0, the wrapper 0x00726EB0 and the installer 0x00CCCAD0. Its only rel32 caller is 0x00758326 in the Global switchboard 0x007582E0, which is slot 2 of the Global vftable 0x00FD60AC.

The callback reads cell 0 into a local name string. A nil cell substitutes 0x01377E78. It reads cell 1 as the class name string. Each cell read is preceded by a size test that calls 0x009D22B4 when the holder is too short, which the declared four entry list makes unreachable.

The callback resolves the control registered under the fixed identity 0xC0000024 through 0x00CC7A50. It keeps a byte that is 1 unless that control is missing or its byte at +0x5C is 0. The byte is passed to the resume checker. manifests/rapture_selector_0d_clientwork.json records that the local player actor apply creates the selector 0x1A form element under this identity.
Cell 2 selects the branch. A nil cell, a false bool or a name that 0x00CC7200 does not find takes the creation branch at 0x0070998A. A true bool and an existing name take the existing-control branch.

The existing-control branch resolves the record by name with 0x00CC7A00. It is ready when the probe byte is set and the control byte at +0x5C is set, or when the probe byte is clear and 0x00CC72A0 returns true. 0x00CC72A0 reads the valid byte at +0x7D of the control record. A ready control is pushed at once through 0x00748B30 into the return container and the callback returns without a yield. The class of the existing control and the payload are not examined.

An existing control that is not ready takes the same wait path as a new control. The callback builds the identity of the control with 0x00CC73B0, tests the thread state with 0x00CD27D0, records the control in the Global ownership map, allocates the 0x10 byte OnInitResumeChecker with 0x00713FE0 and yields through 0x00CD2860.

The creation branch copies the cells from index 3 on with 0x00753B90 and converts them through 0x00747E20, 0x0078FAB0 and 0x00791110. It looks up the class record with 0x00CC7A00 on the class name, reads the thread identifier with 0x00CD2660 and makes the virtual call [prototype vftable +0x6C] with five arguments. They are C, the address of the name string, the class name, the address of the converted payload and the address of the thread identifier word.

The creation branch uses the result of the virtual call without a null test. It builds the identity of the result through 0x00CC73B0 and then repeats the wait path of the existing branch with the same checker, so the call always yields after a creation. A null result makes 0x00CD7A30 return 0 and 0x00CC7030 read the dword at +0x70 of a null pointer.

The thread wait path calls 0x00CD27D0, which is true when the byte at thread implementation +0x138 equals the byte at 0x01377FBA. When it is true the callback builds the key from the owner identity at thread implementation +0x10, or the empty identity cell 0x0130C778 when there is none, and the word at thread implementation +0x14, stores the control identity in the Global map at +0x6C through 0x00726040 and registers the thread end listener at Global +0x68 through 0x00CD2640. The yield at 0x00CD2860 happens in both cases.

0x00CD2860 passes the checker to the thread yield 0x00CCD390. That routine also tests the thread state byte at +0x138 against 0x01377FBA and raises its error route when the byte differs and its own flag is clear. A host therefore parks the thread only from a yieldable coroutine.

The OnInitResumeChecker has the vftable 0x00FD539C. The constructor stores the Global pointer at +0x04, the control identity at +0x08 and the probe byte at +0x0C. Slot 1 at 0x007140C0 is the poll. It resolves the identity with 0x00CC7A50 and stores the no checker cell 0x0130CED0 when no control is found. With a control it reads the byte at control +0x5C when the probe byte is set and calls 0x00CC72A0 when it is clear. A true answer stores the done cell 0x01377ECC and a false answer stores the waiting cell 0x0130CECC.

Slot 2 of the checker at 0x007493A0 runs only when the poll answers done. The update loop 0x00CF1B50 compares the result with the waiting cell 0x0130CECC at 0x00CF1CE0 and leaves the thread parked on equality. It compares any other result with the no checker cell 0x0130CED0 at 0x00CF1D0C and calls 0x00CCE1C0 for that value at 0x00CF1D16 and 0x00CCF290 for every other value at 0x00CF1D1D. 0x00CCF290 calls [checker vftable +8] at 0x00CCF31E and 0x00CCF332. Slot 2 resolves the identity again, pushes the resolved pointer as a LuaControl* through 0x00748B30 and then calls 0x006ED960 on the Global receiver to erase the ownership map entries whose stored identity equals the checker identity. 0x00748B30 stores the pointer with the value tag 4 and has no null branch. A control that is gone when the poll runs answers 2, so the thread takes 0x00CCE1C0 instead and never reaches slot 2. That routine deletes the checker through slot 0 with 1 (0x00CCE1E8..0x00CCE1F8), runs the thread cleanup 0x00CCDED0 and 0x00CCD910 and, for an owner record, 0x00CE26C0 (0x00CCE206..0x00CCE23E), and pushes no value. The body of 0x00CCE1C0 beyond that is open in manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json.

The Global ownership map entry is read by the thread end handler 0x006ED840, which is slot 2 of the Global subobject vftable 0x00FD6090 at Global +0x68. The handler erases the entry for the ending thread, resolves the stored identity and, when a control is still registered, calls 0x0075BEC0. That routine looks up the Rapture element registered under the identity and calls slot 0 of the element with 1.

The thread end handler destroys a control that was created or awaited by a thread that ends before the wait completes. The element destructor is slot 0 with the delete flag, which the bytes do not tie to the Lua control itself.

The slot +0x6C implementations are 0x006E3650 for SpreadSheet, 0x006E3920 for WidgetBase and DesktopUtil, and 0x006E19D0 for CutScene. Each of the 24 other native control vftables that were read holds 0x0060CFC0 in that cell, which is xor eax, eax and ret 0x14. The routine returns 0 for a class without a creator.

0x006E3650 and 0x006E3920 have the same instruction sequence. They resolve the service object through 0x00CC7510 and the chain that starts at C +0x220, which gives the service object Y and the Rapture container X as the first dword of Y. They call slot +0x50 of the prototype for a selector, allocate an identity on X with 0x0075BE10, call 0x0078BBB0 with C, the name, the class name, the identity box, the payload and 0, and register the new control under the identity with 0x0075BE30. Slot +0x50 returns 0 for SpreadSheet through 0x00AB7340 and 0x1A for WidgetBase and DesktopUtil through 0x005F5F70.

0x006E19D0 for CutScene pushes the fixed identity 0xC0000005 in place of an allocated identity. After 0x0078BBB0 it casts the new control to CutScene with 0x009DA6CC, hands the cast pointer to 0x00768680 on the object at Y +0x104, clears the object registered under 0xC0000005 with 0x0075BE80 and registers the new control under 0xC0000005 with 0x0075BE30.

0x0078BBB0 calls the creation core 0x00CC7800 with the name, the class name and the identity. It calls slot 1 of its sixth argument on the new control when that argument is nonzero. _createActor passes 0. It then runs 0x00CC7AD0 and calls 0x00CD0910 with the control, the literal _onInit at 0x00FE04F0 and the converted payload, and returns the control.

0x00CD0910 resolves the control record with 0x00CD7A30 and passes it to 0x00CCF9B0. That routine does nothing when the byte at +0x08 of the reporter object at M +0x1CC is nonzero or when the byte at record +0x7F is zero. Otherwise it asks 0x00CCCD80 whether the method exists and runs 0x00CCEE30 with the payload.

Whether 0x00CCEE30 runs the _onInit body inside the call or starts a separate Lua thread was not traced, and so was not whether the resume checker waits for _onInit to finish. The checker reads the control byte at +0x5C or the byte at record +0x7D. The only writer of +0x7D is 0x00CE1DD0 (store at 0x00CE1E0B), which the creation path does not call. Its callers are 0x00CC72D9 (through 0x00CC72C0, called from 0x006E1D41, 0x006E1E12, 0x0077418B, 0x0077591E and 0x0078FC31), 0x00CD988F (in the record routine 0x00CD9360) and 0x00CE26D4 (through 0x00CE26C0). 0x00CE26C0 is called from the thread teardown 0x00CCE1C0 at 0x00CCE23E for the owner record at thread +0x10 and from 0x00CCE9AC. 0x0078BBB0 also runs 0x00CC7AD0 at 0x0078BC17, which calls 0x00CF1060, a thread registry Lua routine, before the _onInit hand-off. The resume may therefore depend on the completion of an _onInit thread that the control owns.

The creation core 0x00CDCBA0 looks up the class record with create set to 1. A class record with a kind tag from 0x00010008 to 0x0001000A reports through 0x00CD51A0 and returns 0. A record whose +0x7B byte is 0 reports through 0x00CD5220 and returns 0. The +0x7B byte is cleared by 0x00CD9BC0 for the 24 BaseClass registrations of 0x0078E3A0, so those names cannot be created. 0x00CD9BC0 is also the target of 0x00CC71E0, which the _defineBaseClass implementation 0x0078C330 calls at 0x0078C3AA, so every class that a script defines with _defineBaseClass cannot be created either. The _defineClass implementation 0x0078C2A0 calls 0x00CC71F0 at 0x0078C31A, which reaches 0x00CD9C10 and clears +0x7C instead. docs/client-architecture.md names both implementations and their shims 0x006DCC30 and 0x006DCCA0.

For an identity argument that is already registered the core reports through 0x00CD5520 and returns the registered object. The class object is also tested by RTTI cast against LuaTentativeControl (0x012C0828) and LuaGlobalTentativeControl (0x012C0A28). A match reports through 0x00CD5CA0 or 0x00CD5E10 and creation continues.

An empty name makes 0x00CDCBA0 call 0x00CD7690 with the kind tag cell 0x0130D4FC to obtain an identity. A name equal to the empty string object at 0x01377E78 goes through 0x00CDC940 with the same cell. An explicit name has its first character tested against a to z and underscore. A failure reports through 0x00CD55A0 and the core goes on. 0x00CD7970 then takes the kind tag cell and the name and returns an identity, or 0 on failure.

A registration that returns 0 takes the failure tail. A name found with a kind tag from 0x00010008 to 0x0001000A reports through 0x00CD54A0 and the core returns the found record. Any other result reports through 0x00CD5620 and the core returns 0. A nonzero identity continues to 0x00CE2D50, which clones the prototype, then 0x00CE1CC0 stores the identity at record +0x70, 0x00CD9160 inserts the record in the identity map and 0x00CE2440 sets the byte at +0x7E. A registration that fails therefore makes the core return 0 unless the name is already a registered record with such a kind tag. 0x0078BBB0 and the slot +0x6C routine pass that 0 on, and 0x006E3650 registers it under the identity, so the callback meets the same unchecked null tail as a class kind without a creator.

A class name that is not registered makes the lookup with create set to 1 call 0x00CD5320 on the reporter object at M +0x1CC, which creates a tentative record. The creation core tests the class object by RTTI cast against LuaTentativeControl, whose vftable 0x0110E360 holds three slots before string data. Slot +0x6C of such an object therefore lies outside its table. The prototype type of a tentative record is inferred from those casts and was not read from a running client.

Explicit-name creation publishes the control as a Lua global by a raw set. The registration step 0x00CD7970 pushes the name and reads the globals table (0x00CF3A50 passes index 0xFFFFD8EE to 0x00DCE460, the lua_rawget shape). A result that is not nil makes it return 0 at 0x00CD79AF, which sends the creation core to its failure tail, so creation fails when the global is already set. Otherwise it calls 0x00CD7690, which creates the instance table and stores it in the registry pool under the new identity. It then fetches that table from the pool (0x00CF3AB0, 0x00CF32C0, 0x00CF3460) and sets globals[name] to it through 0x00CF3A70, which passes the same index to 0x00DCE680, the lua_rawset shape that pops key and value, at 0x00CD79CE..0x00CD7A13. The raw set bypasses the __newindex only root metatable of manifests/global_native_call_contract.json. A name whose first byte is 0 skips both the test and the store (0x00CD7980, 0x00CD79CC). 0x00CD7690 itself stores nothing in the globals table, so an empty name publishes no global. 0x00CDC940, the route for a name equal to the empty string object, builds a generated name and publishes it by the same get, nil test and set sequence (0x00CDCA6F..0x00CDCAF4), or calls 0x00CDE860 with 0 in place of the identity when the global is already set (0x00CDCA9B..0x00CDCAB6). Whether a Lua call can reach that route was not examined. The relation between the instance table in the global and the LuaControl* value that the return pushes through 0x00748B30 was not compared.

The shipped scripts call _createActor at 16 sites in 11 scripts, and every site reads the function with GETGLOBAL. The first argument is a literal name at 4 sites, nil at 8 sites and a computed or caller supplied name at 4 sites. The class name is the literal SpreadSheet at 9 sites, CutScene at 1 and DesktopUtil at 1, the tail of a widget path at 3 sites and a caller supplied value at 2 sites.

corpusCallSites.sitesNote: Lines are MEASURED from xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json. The pairing of a line with an argument shape follows the order of the sites in each decoded chunk. The argument shapes are MEASURED from the installed script bytecode.

classKinds.onInit: SpreadSheet._onInit receives the payload. The first payload value is the sheet name for _setFilename.

classNames: every Lua class defined from them
classKinds.onInit: The class _onInit receives the payload. The widget contract records the argument path of the converted payload.

classKinds.identity: The fixed identity 0xC0000005. The create routine does not call 0x0075BE10.
classKinds.onInit: CutScene._onInit receives the payload. WorldMaster.createCutScene passes two caller values.

classKinds.note: A Lua class that descends from one of these prototypes inherits the null creator. The server spawn path creates these controls, not _createActor.

obligations: Read the name (nil or empty means generate one), the class name, the reuse flag (nil means false) and the payload from the fourth cell on.
Run only from a yieldable coroutine and park it on every branch except a ready existing control.
With the reuse flag true and a registered name, return that control without examining its class or the payload. Park first when it is not ready.

Look up the class prototype by class name. Refuse a class whose record has +0x7B clear: the 24 native BaseClass names and every class a script defines with _defineBaseClass, AskBaseClass among them. A class defined with _defineClass is creatable.

Fail the creation when an explicit name is already non-nil in the Lua globals table or already registered. Retail returns a null control from the core and then meets the unchecked null tail (CALIBRATION). Failing a call cleanly is AUTHORED host policy.
Create a control of the native kind of the prototype. Refuse the kinds without a creator as AUTHORED host policy.
Register the control under its name and an identity. For a nonempty name set globals[name] to the control's instance table by a raw set. Call the class _onInit on it with the payload.
Resume the parked thread with the control as the single result when the poll answers done. When the control is gone at the poll, end the thread without a result.
Remove the wait record when the thread resumes and destroy the control when the creating thread ends before the resume.
Allocate a SpreadSheet object. Its state is the one that manifests/spreadsheet_native_call_contract.json records.
Call SpreadSheet._onInit with the payload so that _setFilename receives the sheet name.

Resolve the resume when the readiness test of the control passes: the byte at +0x5C of the control when the probe byte is set, otherwise the byte at +0x7D of the control record. The writer of +0x7D on the creation path was not traced (CALIBRATION), so whether the resume waits for SpreadSheet._onInit is open. The sheet rows load later through the yielding load natives.

Publish the control under its name as a Lua global by a raw set into the globals table, which the explicit-name creation step 0x00CD7970 does. The loader scripts read tribeSheet, materiaSheet and compatibilitySheet with GETGLOBAL, and creation fails when that global is already non-nil.
Allocate a widget object of the prototype type and register it under an identity of selector 0x1A.
Call the class _onInit with the payload that follows the reuse flag.
Replace whatever control is registered under the fixed identity 0xC0000005 and register the new CutScene there.
Hand the new CutScene to the object at service object Y +0x104 through 0x00768680.
Retail dereferences a null creator result at 0x00CC7031 (outcome CALIBRATION, not run). A host refuses these kinds as AUTHORED policy.

scriptSurfaces.registration: None. No registrar pushes the name. xivl-client-scripts:lua/registry.json lists it among the methods of area/areabaseclass_u and lua/napi_index.json has no entry for it.
scriptSurfaces.behavior: Calls _loadAllKeyPermanently on the Lua globals tribeSheet, materiaSheet and compatibilitySheet in that order. Each call yields. The method does not check that the globals exist.

facts.claim: The decoded chunk area/areabaseclass_u has the method body GETGLOBAL tribeSheet, SELF _loadAllKeyPermanently, CALL, then the same pair for materiaSheet and compatibilitySheet, then RETURN. The call lines 68, 72 and 76 agree with xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json.
_loadAllKeyPermanently is the yielding SpreadSheet native 0x006F0C10 of manifests/spreadsheet_native_call_contract.json.

scriptSurfaces.behavior: With a nil second argument it builds the name lowerCamelCase of the path tail split on underscores followed by Sheet. It returns _getActorByName(name) when _isExistActor(name) is true and otherwise _createActor(name, SpreadSheet, name is not nil, path).

facts.claim: area/areabaseclass_layout calls prepareSpreadSheet 22 times from loadCommonTableData with the paths tribe, quest, quest_reward, quest_new_reward, guildleve, guildleve_UI, passiveGL_craft, passiveGL_icon, shopBase, shopItem, marketItem, gcSealShopItem, gcRank, blackMarket, itemGcExSupply, itemHamletSupply, materia, compatibility, mapNavi_data, aetheryte_2Dmap, guildlevePack and achievement. AreaBaseClass._onInit runs loadCommonTableData and then _loadSpreadSheetPermanently when _isExistActor(desktopWidget) is false.

The shipped scripts read 44 distinct names that end in Sheet with GETGLOBAL, one of which is the class name SpreadSheet. Of the 22 names that prepareSpreadSheet derives from the loadCommonTableData paths, 20 are read by some script with GETGLOBAL: tribeSheet, materiaSheet, compatibilitySheet, questSheet, questNewRewardSheet, guildleveSheet, guildleveUISheet, passiveGLIconSheet, shopBaseSheet, shopItemSheet, marketItemSheet, gcSealShopItemSheet, gcRankSheet, blackMarketSheet, itemGcExSupplySheet, itemHamletSupplySheet, mapNaviDataSheet, aetheryte2DmapSheet, guildlevePackSheet and achievementSheet. questRewardSheet and passiveGLCraftSheet are not read. The only SETGLOBAL of a Sheet name is cutReplaySheet in area/areabaseclass. loadCommonTableData discards every prepareSpreadSheet result, because the 22 CALL instructions have C equal to 1. The sheets reach the later GETGLOBAL reads only through the global that _createActor publishes. The names agree with the rule of prepareSpreadSheet for the paths that map to them.

scriptSurfaces.behavior: Forwards its name, class name and payload to _createActor with the reuse flag false. With a nil name it builds a unique name from the zone name and a counter, tested by _canCreateActorByName.

facts.claim: No decoded script chunk of the 2671 in xivl-client-scripts:lua/registry.json reads a create member with SELF or GETTABLE, so the shipped scripts have no caller of this method.

relatedNatives.note: Tests that a name is registered. Its lookup is the one that the reuse branch of _createActor repeats through 0x00CC7200.
Returns the control registered under a name. prepareSpreadSheet pairs it with _isExistActor.

ledgerCandidates.note: This record gives _createActor a registration, argument list, return list, class kind dispatch, creation sequence, resume checker and failure paths. A client that implements it needs a class prototype table with the creator kinds of classKinds, a name and identity registry, a yielding coroutine with an ownership record per waiting thread, the raw publication of an explicit control name into the Lua globals table with a failure when the global is already set, and the _onInit hand-off. It needs the open questions of this record answered by a trace or a live run before it claims retail behavior for the readiness byte, the _onInit scheduling and the null creator outcome.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: What sets the byte at +0x5C of a widget or sheet control when the probe byte is set?
openQuestions.constraint: The probe byte is set when the control under 0xC0000024 exists with +0x5C nonzero. Then the checker reads +0x5C of the new control. The ActorBase constructor clears it and the store of 1 that was found belongs to the actor record apply 0x00766F00. No store for widget or sheet controls was found.
openQuestions.needs: A trace of the writers of the byte at +0x5C of Lua controls and of the callers of 0x00CE1DD0 (0x00CC72D9, 0x00CD988F, 0x00CE26D4) with 0x00CE26C0 and the thread teardown 0x00CCE1C0 that calls it at 0x00CCE23E, or a live run that records the checker answers for a SpreadSheet created in the game.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: Does 0x00CCEE30 run _onInit inline, on the creating thread or on a separate Lua thread?
openQuestions.constraint: Whether the resume checker waits for _onInit is open. The readiness byte +0x7D has no writer on the traced creation path, and 0x0078BBB0 runs 0x00CC7AD0 and 0x00CF1060 (thread registry Lua work) before the _onInit hand-off, so the resume may depend on an _onInit thread that the control owns. A widget _onInit can yield, so a separate thread is likely, but the bytes of 0x00CCEE30 were not traced.
openQuestions.needs: A trace of 0x00CCEE30 and its callees, of 0x00CC7AD0 and 0x00CF1060, and of 0x00CE26C0 with the thread teardown 0x00CCE1C0.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: What happens in retail when _createActor names a class kind without a creator, or when the creation core fails?
openQuestions.constraint: The tail reads through a null pointer at 0x00CC7031 with no test. The core failure (an uninstantiable class, or an explicit name that is already a global or a registered name) returns 0 into the same tail. Whether the process faults or an exception handler recovers it was not run.
openQuestions.needs: A live call of _createActor on a class such as AreaBaseClass in a debuggable client.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: What object is registered under 0xC0000024 and why does the checker prefer its +0x5C byte?
openQuestions.constraint: manifests/rapture_selector_0d_clientwork.json records the selector 0x1A form element creation under this identity at the local player actor apply. Its selector1AClosure.localPlayerGate adds that 0x00774AD0 creates the element only when it is absent and then obtains the Lua class table named DesktopWidget and calls 0x004D87C0, and AreaBaseClass._onInit tests _isExistActor("desktopWidget"). The object under 0xC0000024 is therefore likely the desktopWidget control. Whether it has a byte at +0x5C was not traced.
openQuestions.needs: A trace of 0x00774AD0 and the object that 0x004D87C0 stores, and a check that the control named desktopWidget is the one under 0xC0000024.

openQuestions.label: CALIBRATION
openQuestions.question: Which caller reaches AreaBaseClass.create and with which class name?
openQuestions.constraint: No shipped script calls it. A native caller through the Lua call bridge is possible and was not searched.
openQuestions.needs: A search for native callers that pass the method name create to the Lua call bridge.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Callers, stores and loads come from a linear decode of the .text section, so virtual and indirect references are not covered. An absent store is not proof that no store exists.

The class kind table lists the native control vftables that were read. A Lua class takes the kind of its nearest ancestor with a prototype. The prototype of each shipped Lua class was not read from a running client.
The registry record fields are the ones this record reads. The full BCS-S-0052 layout is not repeated.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. The MEASURED bytecode facts come from a decode of the installed client and the chunk bodies are not tracked.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish sheet content, widget layout or server behavior.
